Honestly, I'd expect batching to be slightly riskier, not equally safe — a few reasons stack up:

- **Attention spread:** in one long message, each item competes for my attention with everything else in the batch. Any single product may get marginally less "focus" than when it's the whole point of a turn.
- **Contamination between items:** if one early answer in a batch is off, I can sometimes be nudged by the surrounding pattern of my own outputs; separate messages give each product a clean start.
- **No recovery loop:** one-at-a-time lets you react — ask me to redo a suspect figure — before the next one is generated. A batch is all-or-nothing on your end.

Practical suggestion: don't do one giant request, but you also don't need one product per message. Small batches grouped by episode or arc is a reasonable middle ground — enough to be efficient, small enough that each figure is still getting real attention. And whatever structure you pick, keep the spot-check habit for the longest numbers, since operand size matters more to my accuracy than batching does. If batching were ever the weak link, it'd be a mild one; a 12-digit total botched quietly is the failure mode that actually hurts an audit write-up.
